title: Onramp friction & usage-credit experiments roadmap
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Overview:

This roadmap describes a structured program of product experiments aimed at reducing developer onramp friction and improving trial-to-paid conversion through targeted usage-credit policies and UI/UX changes. The scope covers self-serve signups, initial API usage flows (first 3 days), and the credit redemption experience in Console and SDKs. The goal is to increase meaningful activation (defined below) while minimizing wasted credits and preserving unit economics for hosted inference.

Problem statement:

- New developer accounts often churn before generating production traffic because early evaluation is hampered by: unclear cost expectations, slow feedback loops, and lack of guided sample workloads.
- Broad unconditional credit grants improve vanity metrics (accounts created, tokens consumed) but do not reliably increase 30/90-day retained paid usage and can be exploited by synthetic traffic.
- We need a set of constrained, measurable experiments that balance low-friction evaluation with incentives to convert.

Objectives (north star metrics):

1. Increase 30-day active paid accounts by 18% for cohorts entering via product-led channels.
2. Improve ‘meaningful activation’ rate within 7 days from 12% -> 22%. Meaningful activation = at least one routed production-like request (>= 128 tokens input and model selection not dev-only) and one supervised eval run (developer-run prompt set).
3. Maintain or improve hosted per-token revenue by avoiding credit abuse (target <5% anomalous credit usage across cohorts).

Scope & constraints:

- In scope: hosted API crediting flows, Console onboarding UX, quickstart templates, SDK sample apps, telemetry instrumentation, guardrail rules for credit redemption.
- Out of scope: Dedicated capacity commercial contracts, Private on-prem onboarding flows, enterprise sales-assisted migration paths (these will be referenced but not changed).

Experiment themes and hypothesis matrix:

1) Guided credits (tiered, conditional)
   - Hypothesis: Small, targeted credits tied to completing a guided quickstart will increase meaningful activation without increasing abuse compared to blanket credits.
   - Treatment: 500 token credit + a required quickstart completion event (eg. run create-chat with supplied prompt) valid for 14 days.
   - Success metric: +6pp activation lift; <3% fraud signal.

2) Time-decayed trial buckets
   - Hypothesis: Front-loading tokens with an explicit decay curve nudges developers to evaluate quickly and reduces long-tail idle consumption.
   - Treatment: 1,500 tokens delivered as 900 immediate + 600 unlocked after completing an eval within 3 days.
   - Success metric: increased 7-day conversion, reduced idle-credit carryover by 40%.

3) Workload-aligned sample bundles
   - Hypothesis: Bundles that mirror common workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings) will produce higher meaningful evals than unrestricted credit.
   - Treatment: Offer three labelled bundles (Chat: 2k, Embed: 1k, Rerank: 800) with quickstart templates and sample prompt-sets.
   - Success metric: higher per-bundle activation and longer session lengths.

4) Microbilling preview and cost-guardrails in Console
   - Hypothesis: Transparent cost previews reduce surprise and increase retention.
   - Treatment: Inline estimator showing projected cost for a sample prompt + toggle to simulate quantization/warm-cache savings.
   - Success metric: decreased support tickets about billing and higher preference for paid upgrade.

Telemetry & measurement plan:

- Required signals (priority order):
  1. Account_id, cohort, credit_type, grant_timestamp, redemption_timestamp
  2. First meaningful activation event (event_type, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out)
  3. Quickstart completion flags and sample prompt-set run ids
  4. Cost estimator interactions (toggle events) and upgrade clicks
  5. Fraud signals (high throughput from single IP, repeated credit re-creation, synthetic traffic heuristics)

- Dashboards: Product will own an experiment dashboard showing cohort performance, time-to-activate distribution, redemption decay curves, and cost delta vs control. SRE/Finance will have a subset view for abuse and cost anomalies.

Rollout plan and timeline (quarterly roadmap):

Phase 0 — Prep (4 weeks):
1. Finalize experiment designs and commit to metric definitions.
2. Instrument Console events, SDK quickstart hooks, and server-side credit redemption logs.
3. Define fraud detection rules and cost-exposure caps per cohort.
Ownership: Product + Eng-DevEx + Telemetry.

Phase 1 — Guided credits A/B (6 weeks):
1. Launch A/B test with 25% treatment, 75% control for new signups via the webflow.
2. Monitor activation, fraud signals, and early feedback.
3. Stop / iterate after 6 weeks based on success criteria.
Ownership: Product (lead), Growth, Eng-DevEx.

Phase 2 — Bundles & time-decay experiments (8 weeks):
1. Sequential launch of workload bundles and time-decay experiment (split traffic).
2. Coordinate with docs to publish bundle quickstarts and sample prompt sets.
3. Tighten guardrails if abuse rate > 5% in any cohort.
Ownership: Product, DX, Security.

Phase 3 — Console estimator and commercialization pilot (ongoing):
1. Pilot cost-estimator in Console for treatment cohort.
2. Couple conversion nudges (upgrade CTA with one-click billing).
3. Prepare for commercial packaging changes if conversion and unit economics are favourable.
Ownership: Product, UX, Finance.

Safety & guardrails:

- Per-cohort caps: Max 10k tokens exposure per account from experimental credits until fraud checks pass.
- Abuse response: Automatic freeze + manual review for accounts flagged by fraud heuristics.
- Observability: Real-time alert when credit redemption spike exceeds 3x baseline or when cost deviation > 30% projected.

Commercial implications and pricing notes:

- If experiments succeed (target uplift and acceptable unit economics), recommend the following commercialization path:
  1. Convert guided credit into a permanent onboarding bundle (low-dollar, high-guidance) and expose as the default new account experience.
  2. Offer workload bundles as an upsell during sign-up with clear usage-to-cost mapping; bill leftover credits at standard hosted rates.
  3. For enterprise leads, map onboarding credit usage to sales-assigned demo credits (separate ledger) to avoid double-counting.

- Pricing risk mitigations: Run an offline cost-sensitivity simulator (Finance + Eng-Platform) on sampled cohorts before a full commercial rollout. Define a minimum acceptable gross margin contribution per converted account.

Success criteria and decision gates:

- Gate 1 (go/no-go): After Phase 1, if meaningful activation lift < 3pp or fraud > 5% -> stop and iterate.
- Gate 2 (scale): After Phase 2, if 30-day paid conversion lifts by at least 10% and unit economics (LTV/CAC proxy) within acceptable band -> scale to 50% of self-serve traffic.
- Gate 3 (commercialize): After pilot of Console estimator and upgrade flow, if conversion and margin targets met -> productize bundles and update pricing docs and onboarding flows.

Operational runbook highlights (brief):

1. Monitoring: Daily check on cohort dashboards for first 2 weeks of each launch. Pager if fraud/anomaly thresholds breached.
2. Support flow: Dedicated triage tag for onboarding-credit complaints; escalate to Product on pattern detection.
3. Rollback: Disable new cohort grants immediately and revoke unredeemed credits via ledger batch if abuse seen > 10% of treated cohort.

Open questions & dependencies:

- Do we need new legal wording for trial credit expiry and conversion handling? (Legal + Finance decision)
- Telemetry dependency: require additional token-level attributes to be added to the event schema (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Cross-functional resourcing: need 0.5 FTE from Security for fraud rules during the pilot and 0.8 FTE from Telemetry for dashboarding.

Appendix — Experiment matrix (snapshot):

| Experiment | Treatment size | Duration | Primary metric | Owner |
|------------|----------------|----------|----------------|-------|
| Guided credits | 25% of new signups | 6 weeks | 7-day meaningful activation | Product |
| Time-decay trial | 20% of new signups | 8 weeks | 7-day conversion | Growth |
| Workload bundles | 20% split across bundles | 8 weeks | Bundle-specific activation | DX/Product |
| Cost-estimator UI | 10% of Console users | pilot 6 weeks | Upgrade CTR & support tickets | UX/Product |
